resources.title: Notes: reading numbers
resources.body:
A 3-digit number has hundreds, tens and ones.

Example: 347 is read as 'three hundred forty-seven'.

Tip: read the hundreds first, then the tens and ones together.
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Explanation: why zeros matter
resources.body: In 205 the zero shows that there are no tens. Without the zero we would write 25, which is a very different number.
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Question and answer
resources.body:
Q: How do we write 'four hundred six' in digits?
A: 406.

Q: How many tens are in 480?
A: 8 tens.
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Multiple-choice questions
resources.body:
1. Which number is 'two hundred nine'?
   (a) 29   (b) 209   (c) 290   (d) 2009
   Answer: (b)

2. How many hundreds are in 758?
   (a) 5   (b) 8   (c) 7   (d) 75
   Answer: (c)

resources.body:
Q1. Which is bigger: 389 or 398?
Q2. How many ones are in 604?
Q3. Write 'eight hundred one' in digits.

Answers: 398; 4; 801

resources.title: Revision points
resources.body:
- Numbers up to 999 have hundreds, tens and ones.
- Zero holds a place.
- Read hundreds first.
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Notes: place value
resources.body: In 538: the 5 is in the hundreds place (500), the 3 is in the tens place (30) and the 8 is in the ones place (8).
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Notes: base quantities
resources.body:
A physical quantity is something that can be measured, such as length, mass and time.

In the SI system the base units are the metre (length), kilogram (mass) and second (time).
resources.source: Original sample text written for this app

resources.title: Multiple-choice questions
resources.body:
1. The SI unit of mass is:
   (a) gram   (b) kilogram   (c) pound   (d) tonne
   Answer: (b)
